newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX index ends bourse slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: German DAX index ends bourse slightly lower.

text.p: Germany's DAX index ended bourse trade on Thursday marginally lower, shedding some of the gains from the DAX's recent recovery, after Wall Street ended lower overnight and the dollar lost ground against the mark.

Dealers said that volumes in the market were very low over the session and that even small orders were able to move the market appreciably. The DAX closed at 3,351.49 points, down 7.97 points or 0.24 percent.
"The dollar couldn't hold its highs and then the lower Wall Street also hit. There's a bit of consolidation there all right, but the market isn't doing too badly," a trader in Frankfurt said.
The dollar stabilised over the session and helped boost the car sector, continuing a trend seen of late.

Volkswagen AG was strongly favoured over the session and the share price passed the 1,000-mark threshold for the first time, before paring gains slightly to end at 996 marks, up 54.50 marks, or 5.79 percent, at 986 marks after the carmaker forecast that its 1997 profits would outpace sales growth.

Daimler-Benz AG ended up 70 pfennigs, just over half a percent higher, at 130.70 marks, off a session high of 131.85 marks. BMW AG, a market favourite on Wednesday, ended up 37 marks, or 2.63 percent, at 1,439 marks.
Other features in bourse trade included Hypo-Bank, which fell earlier on after a downgrade and ended 3.79 percent, 2.10 points, at 53.30 marks.
In common with the rest of the main banks, Dresdner Bank AG also fell over the session, despite upbeat 1996 figures, and ended down 78 pfennigs, 1.32 percent, at 57.92 points.

Sportswear maker Adidas AG closed the bourse session off earlier highs, up 3.50 marks, or 1.92 percent, at 182.50 marks after it reported a 43 percent increase in first-quarter 1997 sales to 1.7 billion marks.
